title: Self‑tuning batch governor: continuous workload profiling and safe policy application
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a self‑tuning "batch governor" that continuously profiles live workloads and emits conservative batching/caching policy deltas. The governor should propose per‑route suggestions, apply them safely via shadow/gradual rollout, and provide automatic rollback when QoS regressions are detected. Goal: reduce per‑token unit cost by 10–25% for eligible routes without increasing p95 latency beyond SLA.
background: Current autotune prototypes periodically run offline profiling jobs and produce batch configs that require manual review or full rollout. Several users reported regressions when aggressive coalescing was applied to latency‑sensitive routes. We need an always‑on controller that reasons about stability envelopes, adaptive step sizes, and safety checks before committing live changes.
design_decisions: 1) Use dual‑horizon profiles: short (1–10m) for burst detection and long (6–24h) for steady state. 2) Recommend only parameter deltas (e.g., increase max_batch_size by +2) rather than absolute replacements. 3) Two‑stage apply: shadow apply (mirror traffic on a canary path without affecting production tokens) then incrementally shift real traffic using traffic‑weighted steps. 4) Safety envelope enforced with p95 and error budget thresholds. 5) All decisions are auditable and reversible via one‑click rollback.
prototype_findings:
- Spike profiling on prod‑like cluster (dataset: developer-api traces) showed that many routes can safely coalesce into microbatch windows up to 20ms with 8–12% cost savings.
- High variance in open‑loop interactive routes; introduced a "stability score" combining recent p95 volatility and cache hit variance. Routes with stability score < 0.7 are treated as conservative (smaller deltas).
- Shadow apply uncovered a cache warmup penalty on some routes: recommend staged cache priming before full apply.
- Edge case: streaming calls with server‑side tokenization require different batching semantics; excluded from automatic apply by default.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement governor service in runtime orchestration. 2) Start with opt‑in alpha customers and internal routes. 3) Run shadow applies for 48–72h with telemetry comparison dashboards. 4) If shadow metrics are within thresholds, perform staged traffic shifts (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with 30m observation windows. 5) Automatic rollback triggers at any step if p95 increases by > 15% or error rate trades off beyond error budget. 6) Post‑apply retention: maintain previous config for 72h to allow manual revert.
telemetry_and_safety: Metrics to capture: per‑route token cost, batching efficiency (tokens/coalesced call), p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, KV cache hit ratio, and stability score. Safety signals: transient spikes, correlated CPU/GPU utilization, and model output quality regressions detected by existing eval hooks. Alerts: auto‑rollback alerts in PagerDuty for P0 regressions and annotated Slack/Dashboard events for P1.
tasks: Implement profiler: dual‑horizon sampler and fingerprinting
Build recommendation engine: delta generator and stability scoring
Integrate shadow path in router and console visuals
Add telemetry dashboards and automated alerting rules
Run alpha with two internal customers and collect feedback
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with runtime and platform teams. Scoped MVP to per‑customer per‑route proposals and shadow applies.
2026-03-11: Spike complete — dual‑horizon sampler implemented; initial stability score prototype committed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128).
2026-03-12: Design review with PM and Design. Agreed to exclude streaming/tool‑calling flows from auto‑apply. Added cache priming step to rollout plan.
2026-03-13: Instrumentation plan approved. Telemetry tags and dashboards tracked in infra ticket (ENG-278000). Assigned Diego to implementation and Aisha as product lead for alpha.
open_questions:
- What is acceptable default step size for max_batch_size increments? Proposal: 10–20% relative, capped at +4.
- Should model families (decoder‑only vs encoder‑decoder) use different batching heuristics?
- Who signs off for customer‑visible auto‑applies (legal/compliance review for private deployments)?
